title: kbgit.py ext-release tags the main branch as ext-vX.Y.Z from API_VERSION and its changelog entry, and sync carries the tag to the integration remote
goal: kbgit.py ext-release [--dry-run] reads kbext.API_VERSION, refuses (exit 2, naming what is missing) when kb/_self/extension-changelog.md has no entry for it, when the tag exists, when the checkout is not the main branch or has uncommitted tracked changes, or when kbext.py lint finds a break; else it makes the annotated tag ext-vX.Y.Z with the changelog entry as its message, and --dry-run prints the tag and the message and writes nothing. kbgit.py sync --push sends ext-v tags with the commits they point at; kbgit.py publish sends them to the public home. plugin.md section 4 names ext-v tags beside census tags as the channel a group pins (the first version is this story's gate).

run:
import subprocess,sys; sys.path.insert(0,"_tools"); import kbext
tags=lambda: subprocess.run(["git","tag","--list","ext-v*"],capture_output=True,text=True,check=True).stdout
before=tags(); r=subprocess.run([sys.executable,"_tools/kbgit.py","ext-release","--dry-run"],capture_output=True,text=True)
assert r.returncode==0 and "ext-v"+kbext.API_VERSION in r.stdout, (r.returncode,r.stdout,r.stderr)
assert tags()==before, "dry run made a tag"

gates.question: Which version does the first ext tag carry?
gates.reason: groups inside and outside the organization adopt from day one and only a major may break them; a 0.x series would promise nothing until 1.0
